name: FlippingToTokenPerSecond
summary: Record 6's Decode-8 (AlternatingChain, n32sp) and record 5's Prefill-128 (n32a4) with fewer and cheaper refreshes. Decode-8: masks folded into the Chebyshev series, two heads per lane block (softmax on SparseB-256), scores folded into the Goldschmidt recursion, lighter GELU / exp / LayerNorm seeds, replanned on n32sp (87 refreshes per token instead of 99); dense and SPRU raise drops ending EvalMod on the alternating region's top pair; CutMax's centring masks at a usable plaintext scale (no deterministic wrong argmax). Prefill-128: folded masks, one rotation per window, q.K^T and P.V products relinearized once per sum, more refresh pairs, lighter GELU / exp. Both: exact base conversions in their own kernels, one-prime rescales and fused relinearization-rescales, SPRU's product fused, eager rescales, element-wise chains in one pass. Record 6's client and parameters; Decode-8 asks for four more rotation keys of record 6's kind.

ckks.chain: Decode-8: n32sp (record 6), 51 Q + 13 special primes, every prime < 2^28, dnum 4, log QP 1728.55. Prefill-128: n32a4 (record 5), log QP 1733.26. log_qp above is the larger; record 6's client bounds every dense-secret key at 1734 bits
